messages.subject: reset update
parts:
Hello

Is there a way to reset update button? I have a main panel within a tab that has contents depending on the length of the input from side panel. Something like

UI.R
....
conditionalPanel("input.slc_aetracker_sub_split.length ==2",
                                     xx1
                            ),
conditionalPanel("input.slc_aetracker_sub_split.length ==1",
                                     xx1
                            ),
....

Every time I choose different numbers of input, the graphs and tables on main panel will automatically appear. However, I want them to be blank until I push the update button. And I thought the best way is to reset the update button. How do I do that?

Thank you a lot.

messages.author: 786c3f8c5caf6038
messages.subject: Re: reset update
parts:
Thanks for the fast reply!

I added eventReactive, but still have the same problem. So below I extracted my problem and made an example.This might explain my question better.

UI.R

shinyUI(fluidPage(
 
  titlePanel("Conditional panels UI"),
 
  column(4, wellPanel(
    sliderInput("n", "Number of points:",
                min = 10, max = 200, value = 50, step = 10)
  )),
 
  column(5,
         "The plot below will be not displayed when the slider value",
         "is less than 50.",
        
         # With the conditionalPanel, the condition is a JavaScript
         # expression. In these expressions, input values like
         # input$n are accessed with dots, as in input.n
         actionButton("go", "Go"),
         conditionalPanel("input.n >= 50", # 'input.n >= 50|input.n ==10'
                          plotOutput("scatterPlot", height = 300)
         ),
         conditionalPanel("input.n <40", # 'input.n >= 50|input.n ==10'
                          plotOutput("scatterPlot1", height = 300)
         )
        
  )
))


Server.R:
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
 
 
  randomVals <- eventReactive(input$go, {
    runif(input$n)
  })
 
  output$scatterPlot <- renderPlot({
    input$go
    isolate<- ({
      x <- rnorm(randomVals())
      y <- rnorm(randomVals())
      plot(x, y)
    })
  
  })
 
  output$scatterPlot1 <- renderPlot({
    input$go
    isolate<- ({
     
    x <- rnorm(randomVals())
    y <- rnorm(randomVals())
    plot(x, y)
    })
  })
 
 
 
 
})


When I change n from say 60 to 20, the graph automatically updates, which I do not want. Should I use eventReactive in a different way?

Thank you!

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: reset update
parts:
It's not that the graph updates when you change from 60 to 20. Rather, it's that both graphs update when you hit the Go button, and moving from 60 to 20 hides one graph and reveals the other.

Instead of two different plotOutputs, how about a single plotOutput whose code checks the value of input$n, and makes one plot or another?

messages.author: 786c3f8c5caf6038
messages.subject: Re: reset update
parts:
Got it. Yes that would be ideal. However, in my app, both the layout and number of graphs that show on the main panel would be different based on the number of inputs, so it is hard to make these changes in server.R, which is why I am using conditional panel in UI.R.

Thanks to your link(http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/action-buttons.html), I learned from pattern 5 and was able to implement "reset on input change", now if the number of input changes, the plot simply reset to blank, which is what I wanted. 

Thank you SO much!
